newsitem.title: UK: London platinum higher on Russian supply worries.
newsitem.headline: London platinum higher on Russian supply worries.

text.p: Platinum and palladium prices moved higher on Monday amid concerns Russian supplies might be further delayed, but dealers said the market was beginning to look slightly top-heavy.
"Platinum is the flavour of the day again while there is a squeeze in place on the liquidity," said one London dealer.
"Hopefully we won't see the lows again (in platinum) but I think perhaps we are a bit...high," he added.
Gold followed platinum initially, but momentum quickly stalled and prices fell back to below $342.00 an ounce. Bullion was fixed barely changed at $342.15 from $342.10 on Friday.

Prices did not react early to news from Tokyo that Russian central bank officials may be visiting this week to discuss issuing gold-backed bonds. But a dealer said, "If you securitise gold it's partly bullish because it can't be sold."
The forward platinum market remained tight, with one-month lease rates hovering around 10 percent, dealers said. Borrowing interest was clustered in short periods.
"There is still tightness out there but immediately when we see liquidity get back into the market we will probably see platinum fall back about four, five dollars," said the dealer.
Platinum was quoted $2.50 up on the day at $380.00 an ounce after jumping to $382.50 last week from a low of $354.00.
Palladium gained $4.00 on the back of platinum to $156.25 bid, but it was shy of challenging its recent high of $161.50.

Fuelling the market were perceptions that Russian exports, delayed since December, were nowhere near resumption as Moscow battled with bureaucratic snags and tried to overhaul its archaic precious metals market.
Last week the market was unnerved by rumours that Russia might have faltered on a gold swap for platinum and palladium with Union Bank of Switzerland. No details have yet emerged.
While the uncertainty continued, platinum had the potential to jump by $5, $10 or even more in the near term, dealers said.
Gold dealers were puzzled by a Japanese official's comments that Russia wanted to issue gold-backed bonds.
By 1030 GMT bullion was indicated at $342.00/$342.50 an ounce against Friday's close of $342.20/$$342.70.
"There may be attempts to try to push it down to the recent low of $336 and increases in open interest on Comex point to big short positions again," said a dealer.
On the upside, $345 was likely to be a strong barrier.
Silver was static at $4.74/$4.76 an ounce.
